_meta.name: draw-dialect
_meta.status: DRAFT — the compact 2D description a technical drawing (DXF/DWG) is read into. Shipped with the DXF-first reverse path (ADR-062) and grown with contour chaining + the direct-buildable gate (ADR-064).
_meta.consumed_by: cad-planner/drawing/{contour,pairing,lowering}.py, the `analyze_drawing` MCP tool, and the model itself (get_recipe('reverse') tells it how to read this)
_meta.role: The reverse path's evidence layer. It reports deterministic FACTS ONLY — no feature classification, no 3D inference, no confidence scores. Interpretation belongs to the recipe, and everything that CANNOT be interpreted deterministically is reported as a gap rather than guessed.
_meta.size_is_a_contract: Payload cost is first-class. Loops reference the view's own primitive arrays by INDEX rather than repeating geometry, exact duplicates are dropped at emit time, and the direct-buildable path hands the model a ~10-line summary instead of a contour it would have to echo back.

artifact.analysis_version: string — dxf_read.ANALYSIS_VERSION. A new version writes a new artifact file; the same version overwrites in place.
artifact.source: { file, sha256, bytes, converted_from? } — `converted_from` names the .DWG when SolidWorks produced the DXF. The hash is what lets a later build re-derive from the SAME input without a cache.
artifact.config: { projection, k_factor } — the conventions from config.json that were IN FORCE for this read, recorded so a re-read with different settings is detectable.

sheet.scale_factor: number — DIMLFAC. TRUE value = paper value x this. ALREADY APPLIED to every dimension, view size and geometry coordinate in this artifact; it is reported so the model can see the sheet was 1:2, never so it can multiply again.
sheet.paper_box: [x0, y0, x1, y1] — the sheet frame, in PAPER mm

artifact.alignment: array of { a, b, shares: 'x'|'y' } — two views sharing a paper-axis span are a projection pair. Convention-independent; only the SIGN needs config.projection.
artifact.dimensions: array of { value, kind, defpts, view?, measures?, text? } — `value` is TRUE (scaled). `measures` links a radius/diameter dim to the primitive it measures ('v0:c1').
artifact.notes: array of { text, at, view? } — free text outside the title block (e.g. a bare '2 mm' thickness note, section labels)
artifact.user_description: string or null — filled in BY HAND when the author described the part. Research pool only; the build flow never reads it.

view.role: one of covered.view_roles — 'annotation' marks a cluster that is drafting furniture (a section arrow head), not a view. Marked, never deleted: deleting by size would take a 2 mm thickness view with it.
view.paper_box: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PAPER mm — the coordinate space the bend notes' `at` lives in
view.dropped_duplicates: integer (omitted when 0) — exact-duplicate primitives removed at emit time. The SolidWorks DWG→DXF route is lossless but ADDITIVE: it re-emits a section view's boundary geometry. Duplicates make every shared endpoint look like a degree-4 junction, which stops the chainer dead.

geometry.lines: array of { x1, y1, x2, y2, c } — view-local TRUE mm, origin at the view box's lower-left
geometry.arcs: array of { cx, cy, r, a1, a2, x1, y1, x2, y2, dir, c } — a1/a2 are DEGREES (a DXF ARC always runs CCW from a1 to a2, hence dir=1); x1..y2 are the resolved endpoints, so an arc maps 1:1 onto the IR's `arc` profile primitive with no trigonometry
geometry.circles: array of { cx, cy, d, c } — d is the DIAMETER

view.loops: array of loop objects (see `loop`) — the CLOSED contours found by chaining
view.open_chains: array of { id, class, seq } — maximal chains that did NOT close. An open chain is a segment belonging to no contour: a bend line, a centre line, or (in an ortho view) a silhouette fragment stopped by a T-junction.

loop.class: one of covered.edge_classes — chaining is per class; a loop never mixes classes
loop.role: one of covered.loop_roles — `outer` = contained by no other loop; `inner` = contained. By point-in-polygon containment, which is measurement, not interpretation.
loop.parent: loop id or null — the SMALLEST loop containing this one, so an island inside a hole is representable
loop.area: number — mm^2, ABSOLUTE, with each arc's circular-segment bulge included exactly (verified: f-1's 100x60 outline with an R10 corner and a 4 mm chamfer = 5970.5398 = 6000 − 21.4602 − 8.0)
loop.bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in view-local TRUE mm
loop.seq: array of [code, index, dir] — code is one of covered.seq_codes, index points into the matching `geometry` array, dir is +1 when the primitive is traversed from its stored start to its stored end and -1 when reversed. Consecutive entries share an endpoint exactly; that is what closes the contour on rebuild.

bend_note.rot: number — the annotation's own DXF rotation in degrees; defines its local up axis
bend_note.bend_line: { seg: [code, index], class, note_offset, in_loop } — present when the note matched exactly one line. `in_loop` true means the match landed on a line that IS part of a closed contour, which a bend line never should be: suspicious, kept for observation.
bend_note.unpaired: { reason: one of covered.unpaired_reasons, candidates: [[code, index], …] } — present INSTEAD of bend_line. Never a guess: repairing a wrong bend costs a delete plus a full re-create (no sketch-entity move/delete tool exists), and a wrong fold is invisible to volume, area and topology alike.

direct_build._role: Not part of the artifact — the verdict `lowering.assess` returns for it, and the reason the tool has two result shapes at all. The reader decides; the model is never asked to choose before it has seen any geometry.
direct_build.reason: one of covered.gate_reasons when direct is false — a reason the DRAWING does not force a decision, never an error
direct_build.summary: { flat_view, blank{size,outer_segments,area_mm2,cutouts}, thickness{value_mm,source}, bends[], skipped_bends[], k_factor, expected{volume_m3}, fixed_point_mm } — what the model judges the build on. The contour itself stays out of it.
direct_build.scope_v1: Sheet-metal FLAT PATTERNS. A plain plate is excluded on purpose (thickness source and which view carries the profile are interpretive). Failing the gate costs nothing: the caller falls back to the full analysis, which is the pre-existing behaviour.

covered._note: CONTRACT: every ARRAY here is machine-diffed against the matching frozenset in cad-planner/drawing/*.py by tests/test_draw_contract.py — both directions, exact set equality. Adding a token on one side alone FAILS the gate. Everything else in this file is prose and is deliberately NOT checked (mirrors feature-graph.schema.json's own contract/prose split).

known_limits.chaining: Tier A only — strict degree-2 endpoint chaining. Solves flat patterns completely; leaves ORTHO views partly chained, because a feature silhouette ending mid-edge on the outline is a T-junction (degree 3) and the chainer refuses to guess there. Tier B (planar arrangement: split at interior touch points, then walk faces by leftmost turn) is a separate job — ADR-064.
known_limits.bend_note_rotation: The note-above-the-line rule is generalised through the note's own rotation, but only rotation 0 has been observed. See logs.md KNOWN RISKS.
known_limits.hatch: HATCH entities are dropped (they are not part geometry). Verified they are real HATCH entities in the samples, not exploded line fans.
